main_body: Altar block: a large white upper area holding a lilac panel with a gold cross, a gold lip and brown shadow line, a purple front face with a gold cross and a gold base line, and a grey stone plinth.
top_band: White area, rows 11-23, flat, with a lilac panel and cross that read as a vertical hanging. A gold band at rows 24-25 and a brown line at row 26 mark the edge.
evidence: The white region is nearly as tall as the whole altar and has a face-on lilac panel with an upright cross, so it reads as a vertical cloth or backdrop rather than a foreshortened top. Only the gold lip and brown line at rows 24-26 suggest an edge. The purple front face is flat, with painted stripes and a cross and no inset. The grey strip on the left reads as a flat side or wall piece. The result is closer to a front elevation with a hat than a clear 3/4 block, and the top is not much shorter than the front face.

style.evidence: The white area (about 18x13 px) and the lilac and purple panels are flat fills with no grain or speckle. Each material has only 2-3 tones (purple, gold, grey stone). There is no tinted outline, and forms are separated by hard colour blocks. Tiles carry only about 2-4 colours, well below the stall and well references.
